title: TENIR-Gov: Governance Middleware for AI-Enabled Operational Systems
description:
TENIR-Gov is an open-source governance middleware that sits between decision-producing AI agents and downstream execution environments. It enforces explicit policies, validates operational intents through a neuro-symbolic grammar layer, and persists every governance decision in a cryptographically verifiable Merkle-based audit ledger — independently of any underlying AI model.

The 5.7 line extends published 5.6.1 with: neuro-symbolic validation (LALR(1) grammar + optional LLM fine-tuning), a deterministic policy engine (frozen dataclass contract), a graph-based policy store (Neo4j 5.x), a Merkle epoch audit ledger, an administrative governance plane, a polymorphic UI surface contract, ledger migration tooling, two-kernel composition with HOLD/ESCALATE lifecycle, post-execution assessment (τ⁻¹ partial tau inversion + EVP), a hardened I8 aggregate budget invariant with governor-owned reservation, and CAVE aligned to the epistemic doctrine (Control / Aim / Veto / Epistemics).

5.7.5, the single-host pilot line, hardens 5.7.0: no favorable default for an unmeasured axis, no conclusive veto masked by an invalid measure, no failure after dispatch without a persisted proof of non-execution, and a declarable HOLD bound (τ_K) that refuses alone.
notes: 5.7.5 release metadata (publication status must be checked against the actual GitHub release and PyPI): single-host pilot line, fail-closed hardening of 5.7.0. FM-20 remains open; PySyncObj transport is restricted to explicitly declared development/test environments with loopback-only peers. Production and physical multi-host Raft are unsupported. The Zenodo concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21264802 identifies the all-versions series; the version-specific DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21277138 refers to the historical v5.6.0 archive, not to v5.7.0; the v5.6.1 archive is https://zenodo.org/records/23493054. No DOI is assigned to v5.7.0 or v5.7.5 in these source metadata. The historic 10.5281/zenodo.21264803 article link was withheld from publication metadata pending an authoritative bibliographic check.
